simple.meaning: הָדַף (hâdaph) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to push away or down.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 11 times across Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 2 Kings, Job, and 4 more, beginning at Numbers 35:20. Its contexts include death, righteousness, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָדַף (H1920).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H1920. hadaph הָדַף verb thrust , .push, drive ( הֲדַף in ᵑ7 ; Arabic is ingressus ad aliquem fuit, propinquus fuit , also of time prope accessit ) — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular suffix הֲדָפוֺ Num 35:22 ; Jer 46:15 ; 1 singular suffix וַהֲדַפְתִּיךָ consecutive Isa 22:19 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יֶהְדֹּף Prov 10:3 ; suffix 3masculine singular יֶהְדֳּפֶנּוּ Num 35:20 ; suffix 3masculine plural יֶהְדֳּפֵם Josh 23:5 ; 3 masculine plural suffix יֶהְדְּפֻהוּ Job 18:18 ; 2 masculine plural תֶּהְדֹּ֑פוּ Ezek 34:21 ; Infinitive הֲדֹף Deut 6:19 ; 9:4 ; suffix הָדְפָהּ 2Kin 4:27 ; — 1 thrust, push , subject man, followed by accusative Num 35:20 , 22 (here fatally); subject cattle, figurative of men, Ezek 34:21 (instrumental בְּכָתֵף ; || נָגַח ); push away 2Kin 4:27 (Gehazi, the Shunammite); thrust away (from oneself) figurative = reject , רְשָׁעִים הַוַּת Prov 10:3 (subject ׳י ). 2 thrust out, drive out , followed by מִן of place whence & accusative of person; of ׳י driving out enemies of Israel from Canaan Deut 6:19 ; 9:4 ; Josh 23:5 ; compare also indefinite subject אֶלחֿשֶׁךְ מֵאוֺר יֶהְדְּפֻהוּ Job 18:18 (|| יְנִדֻּהוּ וּמִתֵּבֵל ); & Jer 46:15 (where no plural whence). Hence 3 = depose Isa 22:19 of ׳י deposing Shebna (followed by מִן of station).

occurrences.englishText: If he shoved him out of hatred, or hurled something at him while lying in wait, so that he died,
“ ‘But if he shoved him suddenly without hostility, or hurled on him anything without lying in wait,
to thrust out all your enemies from before you, as Yahweh has spoken.

Don’t say in your heart, after Yahweh your God has thrust them out from before you, “For my righteousness Yahweh has brought me in to possess this land;” because Yahweh drives them out before you because of the wickedness of these nations.
Yahweh your God will thrust them out from before you, and drive them from out of your sight. You shall possess their land, as Yahweh your God spoke to you.

When she came to the man of God to the hill, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to thrust her away; but the man of God said, “Leave her alone; for her soul is troubled within her; and Yahweh has hidden it from me, and has not told me.”
He will be driven from light into darkness,
Yahweh will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry,
I will thrust you from your office. You will be pulled down from your station.
Why are your strong ones swept away?
Because you thrust with side and with shoulder, and push all the diseased with your horns, until you have scattered them abroad;
